title: Network lab 2: Two networks and a router (Filius)
summary: Join two office networks with a router, set every computer's gateway, and trace a packet's path across it.

script.intro: In this lab we join two networks with a router. The key setting is the gateway, and we'll break it on purpose to see what it does.
script.outro: Every computer needs a gateway to leave its own network. Next: names, a web server, and a fault to find.
steps: In this lab we join two networks with a router. The key setting is the gateway, and we'll break it on purpose to see what it does.

Click the router and give interface 1 192.168.1.1 and interface 2 192.168.2.1, both with netmask 255.255.255.0. Now set every computer's Gateway: shop computers use 192.168.1.1, back-office computers use 192.168.2.1.

Run the simulation. From till-1, ping accounts at 192.168.2.21: it answers. Open Show data exchange on the router while you ping, and see the same packet arrive on one interface and leave on the other.
Two networks, one router, and the setting that joins them. Network lab 3 adds names: a DNS server and a web server, then a fault to find.
